name: Medium-chain triglycerides
short: Gastrointestinal side effects, mainly diarrhoea, are common in trials; a review of 21 studies found no other harmful effects. A meta-analysis found a small rise in blood triglycerides.
text: A systematic review of 21 studies of medium-chain triglycerides (MCTs) in Alzheimer's disease and mild cognitive impairment reported that, besides gastrointestinal side effects, no harmful effects were observed, although the authors judged the evidence severely weakened by poorly designed studies, bias and conflicts of interest. In a randomised, placebo-controlled study of an MCT preparation in healthy older adults, the most common adverse event was diarrhoea (100% of participants in the dose-selection part of the study, which 8 people completed, and 75% in the crossover part, which 80 people completed); most adverse events were mild to moderate, and 11% of participants were withdrawn because of adverse events. A meta-analysis of seven randomised trials found that MCT oil did not affect total, LDL or HDL cholesterol overall but caused a small increase in triglycerides, and that it raised total and LDL cholesterol when compared with predominantly unsaturated oils. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
